global_gates: No target source or configuration mutation is authorized.

Native CodeQA MCP is the sole transport for new tasks, continuations, and recoveries; all seven operations, including `list_conversations`, must be exposed and overall_health must succeed, runtime identity requires no desktop auth token or user ID, and a present-but-unhealthy or incomplete MCP blocks Phase 3 while preserving state. A provider that cannot be reached for the repository at all is a different case: an absent MCP surface (mcp-surface-absent) or a healthy surface that cannot reach this repository (repository-not-accessible) may be attested once through codeqa-unavailable, after which Phase 3 completes on the local-source model and the repository completes under the ordinary gates. That attestation is immutable, is refused whenever any task or round is recorded or a dispatch intent is unresolved, and never applies to a failed, cancelled, refused, or empty result from a reachable provider.

Every external start, continuation, or recovery has exact final prompt bytes containing a unique intent ID, a SHA-256-bound persisted codeqa-reserve record before dispatch, and an immediate intent-bound task checkpoint after the provider returns or exact lookup discovers the task.

An unbound dispatch intent blocks another dispatch, convergence, and Phase 3 completion; resume uses list_my_conversations plus get_task and get_task_execution_logs to bind exactly one matching task, while missing or ambiguous identity fails closed and only provider-proven absence plus explicit user authorization may archive the intent as no-task-created.
The reservation contract provides at-most-one automatic dispatch per unresolved intent, not exactly-once provider execution.

Every CodeQA task persists its ID, transport, latest status, and result/round checkpoint; resume inspects the task and any dispatch intent before external state change, and creation is allowed only without an active task ID or after explicit recovery into a fresh generation.

PENDING is poll-by-default and status or elapsed time alone never authorizes cancellation; only get_task plus get_task_execution_logs evidence of a recursive/delegated-work stall and explicit user authorization permit native-MCP cancellation, which must be confirmed and checkpointed as CANCELLED before an explicit intent-reserved recovery whose prompt forbids recursive agent delegation and requires self-investigation by the CodeQA agent.

A pre-existing legacy CLI task may be observed read-only under its original identity only until terminal; CLI is forbidden for task creation, continuation, resume, cancellation, and recovery, and subsequent work explicitly switches to a fresh native-MCP generation.

Every material operation has its own authority, dispatch, fallback, state, idempotency, completion, and recovery evidence; mutating and asynchronous flows require state/side-effect timelines and failure matrices with bounded negative searches.
Generated repository artifacts must be untracked and ignored through exact local Git exclude entries.

Convergence requires full coverage disposition, claim tiers, contradiction closure, all four named core rounds, and two consecutive terminal-successful rounds that have persisted results, are locally reconciled under distinct lenses, and pass the no-material-novelty gate (represented-only items must be verified locally).
Explainer Pro and Workspace Codemap Pro retain their canonical evidence, rendering, publication, and integrity gates.
Repository completion requires publisher readback and a final Git-status digest matching the baseline.
Blocked or unavailable repositories remain explicit in workspace completion.
